prompt: Mailvora's finance team wants purchases and revenue per day for the Dublin days 1 to 7 December 2025 (by event_date). Every purchase counts, one whose first payment was later refunded included. Revenue is the value parameter, read from whichever number slot holds it. Return exactly three columns, in this order: day (the Dublin day as text, in the same form as event_date), purchases and revenue. Return one row for each day with purchases. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per Dublin day with purchases, 1 to 7 December 2025

hints: Next, write the column list of the first step: only what the totals need.
Keep the day and the value parameter of each purchase, read with list_filter, and leave every other column out.
faded_shape:
WITH week_purchases AS (
  -- one row per purchase event of 1 to 7 December 2025 (Dublin days): only the columns the totals need
why_this_works: The first step keeps two columns of one week's purchases, and reading value from every number slot makes the revenue whole.
faded_suffix:
FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
)
SELECT event_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS purchases,
  SUM(COALESCE(v.int_value, v.float_value, v.double_value)) AS revenue
FROM week_purchases
GROUP BY event_date
